plan.title: 2x2 genotype x drug interaction DE + pathway analysis
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question — does the drug act differently in KO than in WT brain tissue — is an interaction question in a 2x2 factorial design (genotype: WT/KO x treatment: vehicle/drug, n=4/cell, 16 samples, 12000 genes, raw salmon counts). This requires fitting a single DESeq2 model with a genotype:treatment interaction term rather than four pairwise comparisons. Track 1 runs QC on sample structure (PCA, sample-distance heatmap, blind VST) to confirm the four groups separate as expected and to catch any mislabelled or outlier sample before the model is fit. Track 2 builds the DESeq2 dataset with an explicit reference level (genotype=WT, treatment=vehicle), fits ~genotype+treatment+genotype:treatment, and reports three results side by side per gene: the drug effect in WT (simple effect at the reference genotype), the drug effect in KO (main effect + interaction), and the interaction term itself (does the drug effect differ between genotypes — the central question). Log2FC shrinkage uses apeglm for the two single-coefficient simple effects and ashr for interaction/combined contrasts that are not a single model coefficient. BH-FDR is applied within each of the three result tables separately, each reported with its own p-value histogram diagnostic and MA/dispersion plots. Track 3 takes each of the three ranked gene lists (by Wald statistic) into fgsea preranked GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark (staged locally) as the primary collection, followed by Reactome and WikiPathways as secondary collections (also staged locally), run separately per contrast per the knowledge-service rule against pooling contrasts. An over-representation/GO follow-up is explicitly gated on there being at least ~50 significant genes in a given contrast, per the flagged rule — the interaction term at n=4/cell has low power and may not clear that bar, which is stated as a caveat rather than silently skipped. All steps report package versions, thresholds, and session info per the reproducibility rule.
